tips.name: First-use guide
tips.announce: First-use guide, {n} of {total}: {title}. Esc closes it.

example.caption: Example: not data from this session

leaderboard.title: The leaderboard
leaderboard.body: The order according to official timing. Click a driver, or their car on the map, to see their telemetry; ↑ and ↓ move to the car ahead or behind.
leaderboard.bodyTouch: The order according to official timing. Tap a driver, or their car on the map, to see their telemetry.

follow.title: Follow a car
follow.body: With a car selected, “Follow” (in its panel) puts the camera behind it; double-clicking the car does the same. Esc goes back to the overview.
follow.bodyTouch: With a car selected, “Follow” (in its panel) puts the camera behind it; double-tapping the car does the same.

timeline.title: The timeline
timeline.body: Click or drag to go to another moment. Hovering shows a preview of what was happening then: the lap, the leader (or the best lap, outside races), flags and nearby marks. Space plays or pauses; ← and → move {seconds} s.
timeline.bodyTouch: Tap or drag to go to another moment; meanwhile a preview shows what was happening then: the lap, the leader (or the best lap, outside races) and flags. Two fingers sideways on the map also move the clock.

estimated.title: What does “Estimated” mean?
estimated.body: Anything Trazada computes or infers, rather than taking it as is from the source, carries this label with a dashed border; press it to see why. Missing data is never made up: it shows “no data”.

analysis.title: Analysis
analysis.body: Race trace, lap pace, tyres and moments of the session, from official timing. “No spoilers” only shows what has already happened in the player.

palette.title: Commands and this guide
palette.body: Ctrl+K (⌘K on Mac) or “/” opens the command palette: type “follow VER”, “lap 30” or “x4”. This guide comes back with the ? button in the header or the ? key.
palette.bodyTouch: The magnifier in the dock opens the command palette: type “follow VER”, “lap 30” or “x4”. Type “guide” to see this guide again.

cmd.title: Show the first-use guide
cmd.detail: Opens it again from the first step: leaderboard, following a car, timeline, “Estimated”, analysis and commands
